# Dodgers win NLDS 2026

Author: Sonja Chen
Published: 2026-10-08T09:21:00Z
Source: mlb.com
Language: en

## Story

Dodgers win NLDS 2026
# Dodgers return to NLCS as Pages delivers clutch October moment
October 8th, 2026
Sonja Chen
ATLANTA -- Coming off a historically poor offensive performance last postseason, Andy Pages went hitless through the first two games of this year's NL Division Series. The small sample of seven at-bats raised some concerns, especially because he missed most of the final month of the regular season due to a fracture in his left hand.
Manager Dave Roberts acknowledged that Pages' performance was some cause for concern. But before the series shifted to Atlanta, Roberts reaffirmed his trust in the young center fielder, a first-time All-Star who became an integral piece of the Dodgers' lineup this season.
"I believe in him," Roberts said. "I feel that for us to win the World Series this year, we're gonna need him to be an active part of our team."
Roberts' faith was rewarded when Pages came through with a two-run single in the seventh inning of NLDS Game 4 on Wednesday night at Truist Park, driving in the winning runs of the Dodgers' 4-1 victory over the Braves that punched their ticket to a third straight NLCS appearance.
"I like being in those at-bats," Pages said in Spanish. "There are times the result comes, sometimes not. But I prepare to be in those spots, and today I was able to get the result."
Said president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman: "My favorite players [are] the ones where you just keep ripping up the sheet in terms of what the strengths are, what the goals are, and they just keep exceeding expectations. And Andy has definitely been that."
The Dodgers have won their past five road postseason games dating back to Game 2 of the 2025 World Series, tying a franchise record. They are 10-1 in their past 11 road postseason games and 14-3 in their past 17. Game 1 of the NLCS is scheduled for Sunday at American Family Field in Milwaukee after the Brewers beat the Padres, 3-1, to clinch their NLDS on Wednesday night.
Bidding for the fifth three-peat in World Series history, the Dodgers have advanced to the next stage in their title defense. Three wins down, and eight to go if they are to reach their ultimate goal.
Pages' breakthrough single was the Dodgers' first -- and only -- hit in 20 plate appearances with runners in scoring position in the NLDS. In all best-of-five or longer postseason series, no team has had no hits in such situations and still won the series.
Last year, Pages' .211 OPS was the worst by any player who had taken at least 50 plate appearances in a single postseason. The poor performance led to him being benched from the starting lineup starting in Game 5 of the World Series, although he made a game-saving catch in Game 7 as a defensive replacement.
Pages used last year as fuel for his breakout 2026. And though he wasn't a big factor at the plate in the first three games of the NLDS, he announced himself with authority in Game 4.
"In this sport, you can't carry previous postseasons into this postseason. Everything is a new chapter," Kiké Hernández said. "Every time you take the field in October, you get an opportunity to rewrite your story."
Atlanta starter Tyler Mahle had been in a groove since the Dodgers tied the game with the help of two Braves errors in the second inning, but his outing came to an end after giving up a single to Teoscar Hernández with one out in the seventh. Righty reliever Didier Fuentes, who had stymied L.A. for 3 2/3 innings in Game 2, got the second out but issued consecutive walks to load the bases.
Right-hander Robert Suarez came on to face Pages, who worked a full count before getting a fastball he could work with. He punched a base hit into left-center, breaking the tie for good.
"You tip your cap to Pages, man," Braves manager Walt Weiss said. "He hit a 100 mph heater back through the middle."

Dodgers beat Braves 4-1 to clinch NL Division Series after Pages’ go-ahead single in the 7th

# Dodgers beat Braves 4-1 to clinch NL Division Series after Pages’ go-ahead single in the 7th

The Dodgers advanced to the National League Championship Series as they seek to become the first NL team to win three straight World Series.

 Los Angeles center fielder Andy Pages hits a two-run single in Game 4 of the National League Division Series against the Braves in Atlanta on Wednesday. Rich von Biberstein / Icon Sportswire via Getty

Oct. 8, 2026, 12:02 AM EDT / Source: The Associated Press

By The Associated Press

ATLANTA — Andy Pages drove in two runs with a bases-loaded single in the seventh inning to give Los Angeles the lead, and the Dodgers beat the Atlanta Braves 4-1 on Wednesday night to clinch their NL Division Series.

The Dodgers won back-to-back games in Atlanta to take the best-of-five matchup 3-1 and advance to the National League Championship Series as they seek to become the first NL team to win three straight World Series.

Pages lined a 3-2 pitch from Robert Suarez up the middle to drive in Teoscar Hernández, who singled off starter Tyler Mahle, and pinch runner Tommy Edman for a 3-1 lead. Didier Fuentes walked pinch hitter Josue De Paula and Kyle Tucker to load the bases. Edman ran for De Paula.

Max Muncy’s solo shot off Raisel Iglesias in the ninth padded the lead and gave the slugger 19 postseason homers with the Dodgers, extending his franchise record.

Dodgers right-hander Tyler Glasnow, making his first start since Sept. 24, allowed only one hit but walked five batters in 4 2/3 innings. After he issued two walks in the fifth, left-hander Alex Vesia ended the inning on Matt Olson’s groundout to second base.

The missed opportunity left the Braves with 18 walks in the series, and none scored.

Glasnow and four relievers combined to give up just three hits. Tanner Scott pitched a perfect eighth before Edwin Díaz got three quick outs for the save.

Mahle, a native of Newport Beach, California, who grew up a Dodgers fan, allowed two runs — one earned — in 6 1/3 innings.

Michael Harris II hit Glasnow’s first pitch for a single before stealing second and eventually scoring from third on a wild pitch that bounced off catcher Will Smith’s chest protector.

The Dodgers pulled even in the second with the help of two Atlanta errors. Shohei Ohtani walked, stole second and advanced to third on catcher Sean Murphy’s errant throw into center field. Muncy’s pop fly into shallow left field was dropped by shortstop Mauricio Dubón for another error, allowing Ohtani to score.

Hernández crashed into the wall while attempting to catch Ozzie Albies’ double off Vesia leading off the sixth. Hernández pointed to his head and neck when talking to an athletic trainer but remained in the game.

Edgardo Henriquez stranded Albies at second. Henriquez allowed one hit in 1 2/3 scoreless innings for the win.

## Injury report

Dodgers second baseman Miguel Rojas was held out after leaving Tuesday night’s 3-1 win during an at-bat in the eighth inning with lower back soreness. Los Angeles manager Dave Roberts said Rojas would not be available off the bench.

Ronald Acuña Jr. started in right field for Atlanta one day after being moved to designated hitter in a late lineup change due to right knee soreness.

The Dodgers will face Milwaukee or San Diego in Game 1 of the NLCS on Sunday.

Associated Press

October 08, 2026 - 3:01am

Andy Pages drove in a pair of runs with the bases loaded and Max Muncy added a solo shot to help the Los Angeles Dodgers beat the Atlanta Braves 4-1.

Pages drove in two runs with a bases-loaded single in the seventh inning to give Los Angeles the lead, and the Dodgers beat the Atlanta Braves 4-1 on Wednesday night to clinch their NL Division Series.

Mahle, a native of Newport Beach, California, who grew up a Dodgers fan, allowed two runs — one earned — in 6 1/3 innings.

Michael Harris II hit Glasnow’s first pitch for a single before stealing second and eventually scoring from third on a wild pitch that bounced off catcher Will Smith’s chest protector.

The Dodgers pulled even in the second with the help of two Atlanta errors. Shohei Ohtani walked, stole second and advanced to third on catcher Sean Murphy’s errant throw into centre field. Muncy’s pop fly into shallow left field was dropped by shortstop Mauricio Dubón for another error, allowing Ohtani to score.

Hitting woes for Braves

The missed opportunity left the Braves with 18 walks in the series, and none scored. Atlanta hitters finished 1 for 23 with runners in scoring position.

“The Dodgers had something to do with that,” manager Walt Weiss said. "They’re going for their third straight world championship for a reason. Their arms just keep coming at you.

“But that’s the post-season. You never know what you’re going to get. It’s very unpredictable.”

Bullpen pecking order restored

# Dodgers one step closer to three-peat with NLDS win over Braves; will face Brewers in NLCS

 By 

 Dean Fioresi 

Dean Fioresi Web Producer, CBS Los Angeles

 Dean Fioresi is a web producer for CBS Los Angeles. He covers breaking news throughout Southern California. When he's not writing about local events, he enjoys focusing on sports and entertainment. 

 Dean Fioresi 

 Updated on: October 7, 2026 / 11:29 PM PDT / CBS LA 

The Los Angeles Dodgers are one step closer to a three-peat following their National League Division Series win over the Atlanta Braves on Wednesday. 

Behind another stellar pitching effort by the Dodgers pitching staff and a clutch two-RBI single from Andy Pages in the seventh inning, the Boys in Blue are now on to their third consecutive NL Championship Series following Wednesday's 4-1 win. 

For the second game in a row, the Dodgers held the Braves to just one run, with Los Angeles starter Tyler Glasnow holding Atlanta to one hit through four and 2/3 innings pitched. He did, however, allow five base on balls to match his strikeout total for the game. 

The Braves scored their lone run in the first inning when Michael Harris II scored on a Glasnow wild pitch after he singled and stole second base, then moved to third on a fielder's choice. 

The Dodgers answered back immediately, taking advantage of a Sean Murphy throwing error and a fielding error by shortstop Mauricio Dubon, which allowed Ohtani to advance all the way around the bases after he walked to start the frame. 

 Ozzie Albies reacts to a pitch during the eighth inning in game four of the National League Division Series at Truist Park on October 07, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. Kevin C. Cox / Getty Images 

Things remained tight from there until the seventh inning, when Atlanta Manager Walt Weis pulled starter Tyler Mahle from the game after six and 1/3 standout innings. He left after giving up a single to Teoscar Hernández, giving way to Didier Fuentes, who got Max Muncy to ground out before promptly walking the next two batters to load the bases for Pages. 

Weis then went to Robert Suarez, who worked Pages to a full count before allowing the single on a 100 mph fastball.

"I've been preparing myself all series for a moment like that, give myself an opportunity, get a good pitch to hit," Pages said after the game. "Luckily I was able to put a good swing on a pitch."

The Dodgers bullpen was lights out on the night, combining to allow just two hits over the last five and a 1/3 innings. After Glasnow was pulled, Manager Dave Roberts went with Alex Vesia (2/3 of an inning), Edgardo Henriquez (1 and 2/3 innings), Tanner Scott (one inning) and Edwin Diaz, who got the save with a shutout frame. 

Max Muncy tacked on an insurance run with a solo homer in the top of the ninth inning off Atlanta reliever Raisel Iglesias. 

## Up next

Atlanta, who finished the year 94-68 as NL East Division champs, will return to the drawing board as they look to return to form that saw them win the World Series in 2021. 

The Dodgers continue their quest to become baseball's first back-to-back-to-back World Series champions since the New York Yankees did so from 1998 to 2000.

They will face baseball's winningest regular season team the Milwaukee Brewers yet again after they took the other NLDS over the San Diego Padres in four games on Wednesday night. Game 1 of the NLCS is scheduled for Sunday.

# Dodgers dominate as Braves’ offense struggles in season-ending loss

With one run in each of final two games, Atlanta falls in four games in NL Division Series. 

Braves first baseman Matt Olson reacts after grounding out with two runners on base during Game 4 of their National League Division Series against the Dodgers on Wednesday, Oct. 7, 2026, in Atlanta. (Miguel Martinez/AJC)

By Chad Bishop

Updated Oct 8, 2026

The Braves’ offense went ice cold at the worst possible time, and the NL East champs are now headed home after losing the NL Division Series in four games to the two-time defending world champion Dodgers. 

A 4-1 loss Wednesday at Truist Park ended the Braves’ season.

“Offensively we fell short,” Braves first baseman Matt Olson said. “Personally, I had some spots I could have come through in and didn’t. Those things are always gonna stick with you.”

Manager Walt Weiss’ team scored eight runs in four games in a feeble attempt to dethrone the reigning champs. The Dodgers scored just 14 times themselves, but that was still more than enough.

# Dodgers beat Braves 4–1 to advance to NLCS

Andy Pages’ two-run seventh-inning single put Los Angeles ahead, and Max Muncy homered in the ninth as the Dodgers clinched the NLDS 3–1.

By The Sporting Page Editorial Staff Published October 7, 2026

Final NLDS GAME 4 · ELIMINATION GAME

LAD 4 ATL 1 Final Saved article snapshot Game updates and statistics ↓

Andy Pages during NLDS Game 4 against Atlanta at Truist Park on October 7, 2026. Photograph published by MLB. · Credit: MLB

## Final recap

The Los Angeles Dodgers beat the Atlanta Braves 4–1 at Truist Park on Wednesday, October 7, winning the National League Division Series 3–1 and advancing to the NL Championship Series. Andy Pages’ two-run single in the seventh inning broke a 1–1 tie and gave Los Angeles the lead for good.

Pages singled off Robert Suarez to score Teoscar Hernández and Tommy Edman for a 3–1 lead. He finished 2 for 3 with two RBIs. Max Muncy added a solo home run off Raisel Iglesias in the ninth.

Atlanta scored first when Michael Harris II came home on Tyler Glasnow’s first-inning wild pitch. The Dodgers tied it in the second when Muncy reached on a fielding error by shortstop Mauricio Dubón and Shohei Ohtani scored.

Glasnow allowed one run on one hit in 4⅔ innings, with five walks and five strikeouts. Alex Vesia, Edgardo Henriquez, Tanner Scott and Edwin Díaz combined for 4⅓ scoreless innings of relief. Henriquez earned the win, and Díaz pitched a perfect ninth for the save.

Tyler Mahle took the loss after allowing two runs, one earned, and three hits in 6⅓ innings. Atlanta finished with three hits and two errors and left seven runners on base.
